Package com.codedstream.otterstream.context.flink

Class FlinkStateContextProvider

java.lang.Object
com.codedstream.otterstream.context.flink.FlinkStateContextProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
ContextProvider
public class FlinkStateContextProvider extends Object implements ContextProvider
ContextProvider backed by Flink's own keyed state — continuously-maintained context (a rolling risk score, a customer profile kept current by a side stream) available at inference time with no external lookup at all, since Flink already has it in local state. This is the "no expensive joins at inference time" pattern: something else keeps this state current as updates stream in, and inference just reads what's already there.

This is architecturally different from every other provider in this module — read this first

Every other ContextProvider (Redis, Memcached, Pinecone, conversation memory) is a free-standing object you can construct once and call fetch(key, ...) on for any key, from any thread, any time. This one is not. Flink's ValueState is scoped to whatever key the enclosing keyed operator is currently processing — there is no "look up a different entity's state" operation, by design, in Flink's state model. Concretely:
  • You can only construct this from inside a RichFunction's open(), via getRuntimeContext().getState(descriptor) — never as a standalone object.
  • You can only call fetch(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>)/update(java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>) from inside that same function's per-record processing (e.g. processElement, asyncInvoke) — never from another thread or outside a record's processing scope.
  • The key parameter to fetch(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>) is advisory only — Flink's state always reflects whatever key is implicitly current for the record being processed, not the string you pass in. If your ContextEngine assembly key doesn't match Flink's actual current key for that record, you will silently read the wrong entity's state (or none) — this is a correctness requirement of your operator's keying, not something this class can validate for you.

Given those constraints, this is normally used outside ContextEngine's parallel multi-provider fan-out (which assumes providers are freely callable from a pool thread) — read it directly in your keyed function and merge it into the request map you pass to ContextEngine.assemble, rather than registering it as one of the engine's own parallel providers. It still implements ContextProvider so it composes with the same Context/flatten() shape as everything else.

Usage (inside your own RichFunction)


 public class FraudDetectionFunction extends KeyedProcessFunction<String, Transaction, Decision> {
     private transient FlinkStateContextProvider stateContext;

     public void open(Configuration parameters) {
         ValueState<Map<String, Object>> state = getRuntimeContext().getState(
                 new ValueStateDescriptor<>("customer-context", Types.MAP(Types.STRING, Types.GENERIC(Object.class))));
         this.stateContext = new FlinkStateContextProvider("flink-state", state);
     }

     public void processElement(Transaction txn, Context ctx, Collector<Decision> out) throws Exception {
         Map<String, Object> customerContext = stateContext.fetch(txn.getCustomerId(), Map.of());
         // ... merge into the request map passed to ContextEngine.assemble, or use directly ...
     }
 }
